description: Helping Hands handheld gripper, Gen 6. Jake (voice): 'It's getting better. I think all the gear mounting and everything should happen actually up above, because I'll be putting it in between my fingers, so I want as little as possible right there in that little niche between my thumb and my index finger. And you see the ones from Generalist? Try just copying those exactly, the gripper shape, with the cutouts and all that stuff. Just identical to those ones. Just try to reproduce them from the images. This is for Gen 6.' Asks: (1) move all gear/servo mounting up above the hand so the thumb-index web stays as empty as possible; (2) reproduce the Generalist gripper fingers exactly from the reference images (shape, cutouts, everything). Build on the latest handheld gripper generation.

results.notes: Jake (voice, with photo): 'Just as a reminder, this is the thing you're trying to copy.' Photo saved at cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_target.png: Generalist handheld gripper. Two yellow fingers with a dark perforated inner pattern (rows of small cutouts), wavy grip profile along the inner edge, tapering to pointed tips; black pivot/linkage plate on top with the gear/drive housing stacked ABOVE the hand; strap around the hand; the thumb-index web stays clear. Match those finger shapes and cutouts as exactly as you can for Gen 6. .

results.identified_issue: Lineage: 'latest handheld gripper generation' = Two Finger Gripper/versions/v005_mirrored_gears (Gen 5 per Scripts/publish_designs.py generations map). Gen 6 is versions/v006_dorsal_drive. Interpreted 'up above' as dorsal (+Y, back of hand), since the pivot axes already run along Y: the gears stack on the same axes above the plane, and each jaw is a plate plus a Ø10 column through the housing floor plus an 8 mm hex that keys a separate gear (separate so the jaw can be assembled through the floor). Housing is split into base and lid with 3 M2 bosses so the gears can be installed. Alternatives not taken: moving pivots further forward along Z (still leaves a hub in the web); remote drive by cable (more parts). Finger outline traced by eye mainly from references/generalist/ziptie_1.jpg; honeycomb cells are 4.6 mm across flats with 1.3 mm walls and a 2.2 mm rim. No Generalist dimensions exist. Dropped from Gen 5: outer finger channel (incompatible with honeycomb plates), hard travel stops, adapter part. STLs are gitignored (*.stl), so only the source, checks, previews and viewer_parts.json are committed; run export_models.py to regenerate. Uncommitted working-tree edits to files I don't own (all untracked and from earlier sessions): Scripts/publish_designs.py generations map (+v006 -> Gen 6), references/generalist/GENERATIONS.txt, Two Finger Gripper/README.md. Gen 5 itself and the publisher are still untracked in git, so the remote gets v006 without them. Unverified: cantilever stiffness, pin bending, strap fit, printability, servo interface.
results.summary: Built Gen 6: the gears, servo and housing now sit on the back of your hand, and the fingers are redrawn as Generalist-style honeycomb plates.
results.detailed_description:
The thumb–index web is now empty except for two 10 mm pivot columns. The housing, both gears and the servo moved up onto the back of your hand, 13–59 mm above the finger plane. A check sweeps the whole 0–22° motion and confirms nothing sits behind the pivots in the hand plane. That space is exactly where Gen 5's hub and motor were.

The fingers copy the Generalist ones from the photos: flat yellow 10 mm plates with hexagon cutouts, a knuckle bump on the outside, a lower blade that swings inward, black pointed TPU tips, and two grey magnet dots. I traced the outline by eye, so it's close, not measured.

Three trade-offs: the fingers now hang from the housing on their columns instead of being clamped on both sides; Gen 5's finger groove and hard stops are gone (you attach with straps through slots, and the servo limits travel); and the servo sits on top, so the stack is taller. Open Gen 6 in the Designs gallery and tell me if the finger shape is right before we print.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake — Gen 6 is up. All the gears and the motor now sit on the back of your hand, so the space between your thumb and index finger is clear apart from two slim pivot posts. The fingers are redrawn to match the Generalist ones: honeycomb cutouts, the knuckle bend and black pointed tips. Take a look and tell me if the shape is right before we print.

summary: The Gen 6 handheld gripper's gear and servo mounting crowds the thumb-index web, which sits between his fingers. Move all mounting above the hand and copy the Generalist gripper fingers exactly from the reference images.
